Rashi on Pesachim 5b:10:1.hebrew: כלפי לייא - שתי מלות: כלפי היכן נוטה דבר זה? הא איפכא מסתברא: נכרי שכבשתו, מסתברא דאסור טפי:
Rashi on Pesachim 5b:10:1.english: On the contrary - [These are] two words: Toward where does this matter incline? Behold, the opposite is logical: [concerning] a gentile whom you conquered, it is more logical that [his leaven] is forbidden all the more.

Rashi on Pesachim 5b:10:2.hebrew: לייא - היכן. וחבירו בברכות בפרק הרואה (ברכות דף נח.): "חצבי לנהרא, כגני לייא" — חרסים שבורים להיכן הולכין:
Rashi on Pesachim 5b:10:2.english: Leya - [Means] "where." And its counterpart [is] in Berakhot, in the chapter [entitled] HaRoeh (Berakhot 58a): "Pitchers [go] to the river; [broken] shards — to where [leya]?" — to where are broken shards going?

Rashi on Pesachim 5b:10:3.hebrew: איפוך - אין לי דאסור אלא בנכרי שכיבשתו, דהוי דומיא דשלך; נכרי שלא כיבשתו — מניין? תלמוד לומר: "לא ימצא". ולא כתב "לא תמצא", אבל "לא ימצא" — לגמרי משמע:
Rashi on Pesachim 5b:10:3.english: Reverse - I have [derived] that it is prohibited only regarding a gentile whom you conquered, as he is similar to "yours"; from where [is it derived regarding] a gentile whom you did not conquer? The verse states: "It shall not be found." And it did not write "You shall not find"; rather, "It shall not be found" implies [it] completely.

Rashi on Pesachim 5b:11:1.hebrew: וארישא קאי - להיתירא: אין לי דמותר לראות של אחרים — בדלא קביל עליה אחריות, כדלקמיה — אלא שלא כיבשתו. נכרי שכיבשתו, מנין דמותר? ת"ל ״לא ימצא״:
Rashi on Pesachim 5b:11:1.english: And it applies to the first clause - [It refers] to the permission: I only have [derived] that it is permitted to see [leaven belonging to] others — [provided] that he did not accept responsibility for it, as [explained] below — [regarding a gentile] whom you did not overcome. [Regarding] a gentile whom you overcame, from where [is it derived] that it is permitted? The verse states: “It shall not be found.”

Rashi on Pesachim 5b:12:1.hebrew: ופרכינן לרבא: תנא מהדר אהיתירא, ונסיב לה למילתיה קרא לאיסורא?! ומשני: להיתירא קא נסיב לה, משום שנאמר בגבולין בשאור ״לך״ ״לך״ תרי זימני: ״לא יראה לך שאור בכל גבולך שבעת ימים״ בפרשת ראה, וכתיב ״לא יראה לך חמץ ולא יראה לך שאור בכל גבולך״ בפרשת בא. ואם אינו ענין להאי ״לך״ בגבולין גבי ראייה, דהא כבר אמור — תניהו ענין ל״לא ימצא״, ודרוש ביה: ״לא ימצא לך״ — אף במצוי אצלך, והיינו שרוי עמך, קאמינא לך דאין חמץ אסור אלא אם כן שלך, אבל אתה מוצא את שלו. וההיא ״לך״ דחמץ לא קחשיב, דשאור וחמץ מיצרך צריכי, כדאמר בביצה (דף ז:) דחד מחבריה לא יליף:
Rashi on Pesachim 5b:12:1.english: And we object to Rava: The tanna seeks permission, yet he cites a verse of prohibition for his statement?! And [the Gemara] answers: He cites it for permission, because regarding borders, in [the case of] leaven, “to you” is stated twice: “No leaven shall be seen to you in all your borders seven days” in Parashat Re'eh, and it is written: “No chametz shall be seen to you, and no leaven shall be seen to you in all your borders” in Parashat Bo. And if it is not needed for this [mention of] “to you” in borders regarding seeing — as it was already stated — apply it to the matter of “it shall not be found”, and expound in it: “It shall not be found to you” — even [regarding leaven] found with you, which means [a gentile who is] dwelling with you, I tell you that chametz is not forbidden unless it is yours, but you may find his. And that [mention of] “to you” of chametz [the Gemara] does not count, because [both] leaven and chametz are necessary, as [the Gemara] states in Beitzah (7b) that one cannot be derived from the other.

Rashi on Pesachim 5b:15:2.hebrew: דבני חילא - גייס של בית המלך, ומטילין תיקון טורח מזונותיהן על העיירות:
Rashi on Pesachim 5b:15:2.english: Of the members of the army - [These were] troops of the royal house, and they impose the burden of preparing their food upon the towns.

Rashi on Pesachim 5b:16:1.english: This works out well - This [ruling] that we said, that on account of [financial] responsibility it is forbidden.

Rashi on Pesachim 5b:16:2.hebrew: למאן דאמר כו' - רבי שמעון קאמר ליה בבבא קמא (דף עא:): קדשים שחייב באחריותן, חייב:
Rashi on Pesachim 5b:16:2.english: According to the one who said, etc. - Rabbi Shimon stated it in Bava Kamma (71b): [Regarding] consecrated animals for which [the owner] bears financial responsibility, [the thief is] liable.

Rashi on Pesachim 5b:1:1.hebrew: ש"מ - מדלא נפקא ליה דהאי יום הראשון ערב יום טוב הוא אלא משום דאסור להבעיר ביום טוב, שמע מינה סבירא ליה כר' יהודה, דאמר לקמן בפרק כל שעה [פסחים כא. וכז:] אין ביעור חמץ אלא שריפה, ויליף לה מנותר; דאי השבתתו בכל דבר סבירא ליה, לוקמיה ביו"ט ויבערנו בדבר אחר — יאכילנו לכלבים או ישליכנו לים:
Rashi on Pesachim 5b:1:1.english: Learn from it - Since he does not derive that this “first day” is the eve of the Festival except because it is forbidden to kindle on the Festival, learn from it [that] he holds in accordance with Rabbi Yehuda, who says later in the chapter [entitled] Kol Sha'ah [Pesachim 21a and 27b]: “There is no removal of leaven except [by] burning,” and he derives it from notar [leftover sacrificial meat]; for if he held [that] its removal [may be accomplished] by any means, let him establish it on the Festival [itself], and he would remove it through something else: he would feed it to dogs or throw it into the sea.

Rashi on Pesachim 5b:1:2.hebrew: וש"מ - מדקאמר שהוא אב מלאכה, סבירא ליה כר' נתן, דאמר: הבערה לחלק יצאתה. דתניא (שבת דף ע.): הבערה ללאו יצאת — שהיתה בכלל "לא תעשה כל מלאכה", חזר והוציאה מכללו ופרט בה לאו לעצמה, לומר לך שאינה במיתת בית דין כשאר מלאכות, אלא בלאו זה לבדו. ר' נתן אומר: לחלק יצאתה — שלא תאמר: העושה ארבעה או חמשה אבות מלאכות בשוגג בשבת אינו חייב אלא אחת, דהא חד לאו איכא בכולהו וחד כרת, לפיכך פרט בה בפני עצמה להקיש אליה: מה היא מיוחדת שהיא אב מלאכה וחייבין עליה לעצמה כו', אלמא לר' יוסי לאו אב מלאכה היא:
Rashi on Pesachim 5b:1:2.english: And learn from it - From the fact that he said that it is a primary category of labor, he holds in accordance with Rabbi Natan, who said kindling was singled out to divide liability. As it was taught in a baraita (Shabbat 70a): Kindling was singled out to teach that it is subject only to a negative prohibition — for it was included in the general rule “You shall not do any work,” and the Torah then singled it out from its general category and specified a negative prohibition for it on its own, to tell you that it is not punishable by court execution like the other labors, but rather only by this negative prohibition alone. Rabbi Natan says: It was singled out to divide liability — so that you should not say: one who performs four or five primary categories of labor unwittingly on Shabbat is liable for only one sin offering, since there is only one negative prohibition encompassing all of them and one karet; therefore the Torah specified it on its own to draw an analogy to it: just as it is distinctive in that it is a primary category of labor and one is liable for it on its own, etc. It is evident that according to Rabbi Yose it is not a primary category of labor.

Rashi on Pesachim 5b:2:1.english: Wasn’t it already stated: “No leaven shall be seen with you in all your borders”? - Behold, houses are implied [in this].

Rashi on Pesachim 5b:3:1.hebrew: לפי שנאמר ולא יראה לך - דמדכתב "לך", משמע מינה: שלך אי אתה רואה, אבל אתה רואה בגבולין של אחרים — כגון נכרי — ושל גבוה, אם הקדישם לבדק הבית:
Rashi on Pesachim 5b:3:1.english: Because it is stated: “And [it] shall not be seen with you” - For since it is written “with you,” it implies from it: Your own [leaven] you may not see, but you may see within [your] borders [that] of others — such as a gentile — and [that] of the Most High, if one consecrated them for the Temple maintenance.

Rashi on Pesachim 5b:3:2.hebrew: יכול - נלמוד ממקרא זה שיטמין את שלו ביד שלא יראנו, ודיו — דהא ״לא יראה״ כתיב:
Rashi on Pesachim 5b:3:2.english: I might [have thought] - We might learn from this verse that one may conceal his own [leaven] in a manner that he will not see it, and that is sufficient for him, since “shall not be seen” is written.

Rashi on Pesachim 5b:3:3.english: And accept deposits from a gentile - For behold, it is written: "to you" [i.e., your own].

Rashi on Pesachim 5b:3:4.hebrew: ת"ל לא ימצא - אסר לך הטמנה, שאף היא בכלל מציאה; ואסר לך של אחרים, דהכא לא כתיב לך:
Rashi on Pesachim 5b:3:4.english: The verse states: “Shall not be found” - [The verse] forbade concealment to you, for it too is included in [the prohibition of] finding; and it forbade [leaven belonging to] others to you, as here “to you” is not written.

Rashi on Pesachim 5b:4:1.hebrew: אין לי - מלא ימצא דאסור, אלא נכרי שלא כבשתו תחת ידיך ואינו שרוי עמך בחצר. ולקמיה פריך: איפכא מסתברא:
Rashi on Pesachim 5b:4:1.english: I have only - [Derived] from “it shall not be found” that it is forbidden, only [regarding] a gentile whom you did not subjugate under your control and who does not dwell with you in the courtyard. And later on, [the Gemara] asks: The opposite is reasonable!

Rashi on Pesachim 5b:4:2.hebrew: נכרי שכיבשתו תחת ידך - דהוי ממונו כממונך, או שלא כיבשתו אבל שרוי בחצרך, מנין? תלמוד לומר: ״לא ימצא״. לקמיה מפרש לה:
Rashi on Pesachim 5b:4:2.english: A gentile whom you conquered under your hand - For his property is like your property. Or [a gentile] whom you did not conquer, but who dwells in your courtyard — from where [is it derived]? The verse states: “It shall not be found.” Below, [the Gemara] explains it.

Rashi on Pesachim 5b:5:1.hebrew: ואין לי אלא בבתים - כלומר, ואם נאמר זה ולא נאמר "ולא יראה לך שאור", הייתי אומר: אין לי שאסור לשהות חמץ אלא בבתים, מפני שהוא מצוי אצלו תמיד — דהא בהאי קרא "בתים" הוא דכתיב:
Rashi on Pesachim 5b:5:1.english: And I have [derived] only in houses - That is to say, if this [verse] were stated and “nor shall leaven be seen of you” were not stated, I would have said: I have [derived] that it is forbidden to keep leaven only in houses, because it is constantly accessible to him — for in this verse, it is “houses” that is written.

Rashi on Pesachim 5b:5:2.english: The verse states: "In all your borders" - It is written in the verse of "it shall not be seen."

Rashi on Pesachim 5b:6:1.hebrew: ועדיין - אע"פ שנאמר שניהם, יש לי לומר: בבתים עובר בכל אלו, דהא "לא ימצא", דמשמע אפילו הטמנה, לא כתב אלא בבתים, ולא כתב בהו נמי "לך" להוציא של אחרים. אבל בגבולין — בורות, שיחין ומערות — כתב "לך", ואני אומר: אבל אתה רואה בהן של אחרים. מנין ליתן קולו של זה בזה וחומרו של זה בזה? ת"ל כו'. ולקמיה פריך: מאי קאמר, דמייתי לה של אחרים ושל גבוה לאיסורא ולהתירא הכא והכא:
Rashi on Pesachim 5b:6:1.english: And still - Even though both were stated, I have [reason] to say: In houses, one violates all of these [prohibitions], for “shall not be found” — which implies even concealing — was written only regarding houses, and It also did not write regarding them “yours” to exclude that which belongs to others. But regarding borders — pits, ditches, and caves — It wrote “yours,” and I say: But you may see in them that which belongs to others. From where [is it derived] to apply the leniency of this [context] to that [context] and the stringency of this [context] to that [context]? The verse states, etc. And later on, [the Gemara] raises an objection: What is [the tanna] saying, that he adduces that which belongs to others and that which belongs to the Sanctuary for a prohibition and for a permission, here and there?

Tosafot on Pesachim 5b:12:1.hebrew: משום דכתיב לך לך תרי זימני - פ"ה: כיון דמייתר "לך", שדייה אלא ימצא. וקשה לרשב"א: דמיתורא ד"לך" גופיה, אפילו בלא [לא] ימצא, מצינו למעוטי נכרי שכיבשתו! ואור"י: דאי לאו מלא ימצא, מ"לך" לא ממעטינן נכרי שכיבשתו, דההוא נמי "לך" חשיבא, וה"א דאתי לדרשה אחרינא; אבל השתא דשדינא אלא ימצא, ממשמעותיה ממעטינן נכרי שכיבשתו — ד"לא ימצא לך" משמע: אפילו במצוי בעינא "לך". אבל עוד קשה לו: כיון דשדינא אלא ימצא, אמאי איצטריך ליה לעיל למדרש "מה שאור האמור בגבולים וכו' אף שאור האמור בבתים שלך אי אתה רואה וכו'"? ותירץ ר"י: דאי לאו דרשה דשאור שאור, הוה מוקי לה למעוטי של אחרים ושל גבוה בבתים כמו בגבולים, ולא למעוטי נכרי שכיבשתו — ודוחק. הקשה רבינו תם: דבשום דוכתא לא מצריכנא תרי קראי לכיבשתו ושלא כיבשתו! בראשית הגז (חולין קלה:) גבי "ביתך", "דגנך", "שדך", וטובא דמייתי התם — בכולהו לא מצריך אלא חד קרא לכיבשתו ולשלא כיבשתו! ותי' רשב"א: דכיון דגלי לן הכא נכרי שכיבשתו לא חשיב שלך, בשום דוכתא תו לא צריך תרי קראי, וממעטינן תרוייהו מחד קרא. וכן יש לתרץ מה שהקשה ה"ר יעקב דאורליינ"ש מעריסותיכם:
Tosafot on Pesachim 5b:12:1.english: Because it is written: "With you," "with you," twice - Rashi explained: Since [the word] "with you" [lekha] is superfluous, cast it upon [the verse] "shall not be found" [lo yimatzei, applying it to mean "it shall not be found with you"]. And the Rashba raises a difficulty: For from the superfluity of "with you" itself, even without [attaching it to] "shall [not] be found," we could have excluded a gentile whom you conquered! And the Ri says: Were it not for [deriving it from] "shall not be found," we would not have excluded a gentile whom you conquered from "with you" [alone], because that [leaven] is also considered "yours" [since he is subjugated to you], and I would have said that [the extra "with you"] comes for another derivation; but now that we cast [the word "with you"] upon "shall not be found," we exclude a gentile whom you conquered from its plain meaning — as "it shall not be found with you" implies: even regarding that which is merely found [in your domain], I require that it be "yours" [for the prohibition to apply]. However, he [the Rashba] further raises a difficulty: Since we cast [the word "with you"] upon "shall not be found" [which refers to houses], why did [the baraita] need to derive above [via verbal analogy]: "Just as the leaven stated regarding borders [etc., your own you may not see, but you may see that of others and that of the Sanctuary], so too the leaven stated regarding houses, your own you may not see [etc.]"? And the Ri answered: Were it not for the derivation of "leaven" [and] "leaven," he would have applied it [the extra "with you" attached to "shall not be found"] to exclude [only leaven] of others and of the Sanctuary in houses, just as in borders, and not to exclude a gentile whom you conquered — and [this answer] is forced. Rabbeinu Tam raised a difficulty: Nowhere else do we require two verses for [a gentile] whom you conquered and [one] whom you did not conquer! In [the chapter] Reishit HaGez (Chullin 135b), regarding "your house" [beitekha], "your grain" [deganekha], "your field" [sadekha], and the many [other cases] that [the Gemara] cites there — in all of them, it requires only a single verse for [both one] whom you conquered and [one] whom you did not conquer! And the Rashba answered: Since [the Torah] revealed to us here that a gentile whom you conquered is not considered "yours," in no [other] place does it require two verses anymore, and we exclude both of them from a single verse. And similarly, one can answer what Harav Rabbi Ya'akov of Orleans raised from "your doughs":

Tosafot on Pesachim 5b:1:1.hebrew: לחלק יצאת - מדקרי לה אב מלאכה. ועוד אומר ריב"א, דלמ"ד ללאו יצאתה לא היה אסור ביו"ט, כיון דאין שם מלאכה עליה:
Tosafot on Pesachim 5b:1:1.english: [Kindling] was singled out to divide - From [the fact] that [Rabbi Akiva] called it a primary category of labor [av melakhah]. And furthermore, the Riva says that according to the one who holds that [kindling] was singled out [merely] for a negative commandment, it would not have been forbidden on Yom Tov, since the designation of labor does not apply to it.

Tosafot on Pesachim 5b:1:2.hebrew: לא אמרינן מתוך - דאי אמרינן מתוך, שרי; אע"ג דבעינן צורך היום קצת — הכא מה שמבער הוי צורך:
Tosafot on Pesachim 5b:1:2.english: We do not say mitokh - For if we were to say [the principle of] mitokh [applies], it would be permitted. Even though we require a bit of need for the day [for mitokh to apply], here, that which he burns is a need.

Tosafot on Pesachim 5b:3:1.hebrew: אבל אתה רואה של אחרים ושל גבוה - הקשה הרב ר' יעקב דאורליי"נש: דהכא לא מצריך תרי קראי למעוטי נכרי וגבוה, דמחד "לך" ממעטינן תרוייהו, אע"ג דתלתא "לך" כתיבי, ובפ' כל שעה (לקמן פסחים כג.) משמע דצריכי כולהו! ובמנחות, בפרק רבי ישמעאל (מנחות דף סז. ושם), קאמר: תרי "עריסותיכם" כתיבי, חד למעוטי נכרי וחד למעוטי הקדש? ומיהו, בספרים מדויקים גרס: חד כדי עריסותיכם — פירוש: כשיעור עיסת מדבר — וחד לעיסת הקדש. וכן נראה, דבראשית הגז (חולין קלה:) דרשינן: "מעריסותיכם" — כדי עיסתכם:
Tosafot on Pesachim 5b:3:1.english: “But you may see that of others and that of the Most High” - The teacher Rabbi Jacob of Orléans raised a difficulty: that here, the baraita does not require two verses to exclude a gentile and consecrated property, since from one instance of “with you” we exclude both of them, even though three instances of “with you” are written in the Torah, and in the chapter entitled Kol Sha’ah (below, Pesachim 23a) it implies that all of them are needed! And in Menachot, in the chapter entitled Rabbi Yishmael (Menachot 67a, and there), it says: Two instances of “your dough” are written — one to exclude a gentile, and one to exclude consecrated property? However, in precise texts the reading is: One is “as the amount of your dough” — meaning, like the measure of the dough in the wilderness — and one is for consecrated dough. And so it appears, for in the chapter entitled Reishit HaGez (Chullin 135b) we expound: From “your dough” — as the amount of your dough.
